intended_object: The space c₀₀ of finitely supported scalar sequences ℕ → 𝕜, seen as a subspace of ℓ²(ℕ, 𝕜) and carrying the ℓ² norm. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation, which uses it as a counterexample to the closed-range theorem when the domain is not complete.
explanation:
The definition takes the preimage of `lpSubmodule 𝕜 _ 0` under the inclusion of ℓ² into all sequences. `Memℓp f 0` means that f has finite support (see `memℓp_zero_iff`). So an element x of ℓ² belongs to the submodule exactly when x has finite support, which the next lemma `mem_finiteSupportL2_iff` states. Because it is a `Submodule` of `lp _ 2`, its norm is the one inherited from ℓ², as the docstring says. It works over any normed field.

This is a specific object built for a counterexample: the standard c₀₀ inside ℓ²(ℕ). Using the index set ℕ is the standard choice for this example, not an unjustified restriction. Mathlib has no definition of this particular subspace; `Finsupp`, mentioned in the module docs, is a different type and has no ℓ² norm.
